title.narrative: Pillar 2 (100%) – Coordination/PSEA/Support Services - Multi-sectorial Needs Assessment Phase III - Support for Evidence-Based Aid Planning and Delive

description.narrative:
ltpgtltbrgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gtLebanon continues to face a multi-layered crisis characterized by an acute economic contraction including exchange rate collapse, rising public debt, soaring inflation, impaired banking sector, political turmoil, and governance challenges inter alia. Humanitarian aid is important to help mitigate the effect of the crisis and give more time to the international community to demand reforms. To ensure that programming responds to the rapidly changing needs and environment on a localized level, it is crucial that timely and up-to-date information is maintained and reinforced. To meet the evolving information needs of the humanitarian community, REACH aims to provide relevant and quality evidence to complement existing evidence-collection efforts and fill important data gaps. lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gt lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gtTherefore, in collaboration with UN OCHA and through the mandate of the UN Humanitarian Country Team (HCT), REACH proposes to conduct a third Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA), consisting of a multi-sectoral household (HH) survey employed among a relevant sample nationwide for Lebanese, PRL (Palestine Refugees in Lebanon) and Migrant households. The assessment aims to inform a better understanding of needs and 2024 response planning and will facilitate evidence-based humanitarian decision-making, planning and action. REACH will lead the overall technical implementation of the MSNA and provide oversight to each phase of the MSNA research cycle analysis of MSNA data and the production of the key outputs. REACH, together with OCHA, will work closely with sectoral and thematic experts across the response, to ensure the MSNA is contextualized and endorsed by all relevant partners. The MSNA will therefore provide data to finalise the joint sectoral and intersectoral needs analysis that will inform the 2024 humanitarian response planning and prioritisation, fulfilling Core Commitment 5 of the Grand Bargain through the conduct of a joint, impartial, and collaborative needs assessment.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gt lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gtThe following outputs will be developed:ltbrgt - 1 final (clean) household data set + analysis tablesltbrgt - 1 Summary findings dashboardltbrgt - Presentations to key stakeholders ltbrgt - 3 multi-sectoral factsheets (including all sectors) (minimum of 1 per population group) ltbrgt - 1 MSNA intersectoral brief.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gt- 1 AAP factsheetlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gt- Presentations and discussions with local communities and authoritieslt/spangtlt/pgt
